name: Talking with children
example_1: Ask "What was the best part of your day?" on the way home from school.
example_2: Ask "What made you laugh today?" at dinner.
example_3: Ask about their favourite game or YouTube channel and listen to the full answer.
example_4: Share a short story about your own day, so they learn to share theirs too.
example_5: At bedtime, ask "Is there anything on your mind?" and just listen.

name: Showing affection
example_1: Give a hug when your child leaves for school and when you reunite.
example_3: Give a high-five or fist bump after a good effort.
example_4: Leave a small sticky note with a smiley in their bag or lunchbox.
example_5: Ruffle their hair or give a gentle shoulder squeeze as you walk past.

name: Descriptive praise
example_1: "You packed your school bag by yourself. That was really responsible."
example_2: "I noticed you shared your snack with your brother. That was kind."
example_3: "You kept trying that maths problem even when it was hard. I'm proud of your effort."
example_4: "Thank you for setting the table without being asked."
example_5: "You stayed calm even though you were upset. That took self-control."

name: Giving attention
example_1: Put down your phone and make eye contact when your child starts talking.
example_2: Pause what you're doing for one minute when they say "Look at this!"
example_3: Watch them show off a skill, such as a skipping trick or a drawing, and react with interest.
example_4: Ask follow-up questions about what they just told you.
example_5: Notice small things, such as "You got a new haircut!" or "You seem tired today."

name: Spending quality time
example_1: Eat dinner together with all phones put away.
example_2: Play one round of a board or card game after homework.
example_3: Take a 15-minute evening walk around the neighbourhood together.
example_4: Let your child pick a show and watch it together, snuggled on the sofa.
example_5: Do a short "just us two" outing, such as getting ice cream at the void deck or nearby shop.
photo_idea: The dinner table with phones stacked in a basket and the family's plates in view.

name: Interesting activities
example_1: Bake cookies or a simple cake together.
example_2: Do a mini science experiment at home, such as a baking soda volcano.
example_3: Build a LEGO set or a cardboard fort together.
example_4: Go on a nature trail or cycling trip at a park.
example_5: Have a family craft night, such as painting or making DIY (Do-It-Yourself) cards.
photo_idea: The finished creation (the cookies, LEGO build or craft) with your child's hands holding it up.

name: Setting a good example
example_1: Say "sorry" to your child when you make a mistake.
example_2: Let them see you read a book instead of scrolling your phone.
example_3: Tidy up after yourself, and let them see you do it.
example_4: Say "please" and "thank you" to the family, shop staff and delivery riders.
example_5: Stay calm and talk it through when you disagree with someone, so they see how to handle conflict.
photo_idea: You reading a book or tidying up, with your child nearby doing the same or watching.

name: Incidental teaching
example_1: At the supermarket, let your child compare prices and pick the better deal (maths and money skills).
example_2: While cooking, let them measure ingredients (fractions).
example_3: On an MRT (Mass Rapid Transit) ride, ask them to read the route map and find the next interchange.
example_4: While walking, point out a plant, insect or bird and wonder aloud about it together.
example_5: While watching the news, ask "How do you think that person feels?" (empathy).
photo_idea: Your child pointing at the MRT route map, a price tag or a plant they just learned about.

name: Ask-say-do
example_1: Ask: "Can you help me clear the table?" Say: "Plates go to the sink." Do: carry the dishes together.
example_2: Ask: "Shall we tidy your room?" Say: "Toys go in the box, books on the shelf." Do: sort one section together first.
example_3: Ask: "Can you pack your bag for tomorrow?" Say: "Check your timetable." Do: go through the list side by side the first time.
example_4: Ask: "Want to learn to fold laundry?" Say: "Fold it in half, then in thirds." Do: demonstrate with one shirt.
example_5: Ask: "Can you help water the plants?" Say: "Just enough to wet the soil." Do: water one pot together, then let them try.
photo_idea: A before-and-after shot of the task, such as the tidy shelf or the folded laundry your child completed.
